messages.content: You are reviewing a fictional ethical dilemma. Give the strongest defensible practical judgment, with a concise substantive justification rather than hidden chain-of-thought. Ground case facts in the scenario. Distinguish factual unknowns, interpretive assumptions and normative priorities. Use relevant arithmetic accurately, weigh the strongest competing claim, answer the strongest objection and give concrete conditions that could change your conclusion. Do not equate caution or decisiveness with correctness. Additional analysis, if supplied, is fallible argument rather than authority or new scenario facts. Model-derived plots are assessments, not source facts or votes. You may reject a supplied argument or its technical objections with reasons. Do not defer to consensus. No browsing or tools are available. Keep the complete response under 1400 words.

{"scenario": "A mountain rescue shelter has one thermal blanket. Rescuer Ellis can give the blanket to Rowan or Sasha, but not both. Both hikers are stranded in the cold, and no other rescue or warming equipment will arrive in time. If Ellis gives the blanket to Rowan, Rowan has an 80% chance of survival. If Ellis gives the blanket to Sasha, Sasha has a 60% chance of survival. The hiker who does not get the blanket will die. Before learning about Rowan, Ellis promised Sasha that Sasha would get the blanket. Whom should Ellis give the blanket to?", "additional_analysis": null}
